title: Construct Uniform Parity Array I
summary: Given an array nums1 of n distinct integers, determine if it is possible to construct another array nums2 of the same length such that all elements in nums2 are either all odd or all even.
statement: Given an array nums1 of n distinct integers, determine if it is possible to construct another array nums2 of the same length such that all elements in nums2 are either all odd or all even. This can be achieved by either keeping the original element from nums1 or subtracting any other element in nums1 from the chosen element. Return true if such an array nums2 can be constructed, otherwise return false.
constraints: For every output position, either keep its original distinct value or subtract another input value from it.
Determine whether all constructed values can share one parity.
Return whether such a construction exists.
hints: If all values share parity, keep them unchanged.
Otherwise at least one odd value exists.
Keep every odd value; for each even value subtract any odd input, producing odd.
Thus a uniform construction always exists under the allowed choices.
editorial: Thus a uniform construction always exists under the allowed choices.

tests.explanation: Keep odd three and replace two by two minus three, which is odd.
Keeping all values already gives uniform even parity.
